title: Chapter 6: Plate Tectonics and Continental Drift

blocks.content: Plate tectonics is the fundamental theory explaining the structure and dynamics of the Earth's surface. It links continental movement, ocean basin formation, earthquakes, volcanoes, mountain building, and geological hazards into a single framework. The lithosphere is divided into rigid plates that move slowly over the semi-fluid asthenosphere due to internal heat-driven processes.
Plate tectonics is the fundamental theory explaining the structure and dynamics of the Earth's surface.

rows: Sub-surface layer over which plates move

items: The lithosphere consists of rigid plates, whereas the asthenosphere is semi-fluid.
Internal heat-driven processes are the primary mechanism behind plate movements.
Plate tectonics unifies geological hazards, mountain building, and continental movement into a single theoretical framework.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Plate tectonics is the unifying framework explaining Earth's surface dynamics and structure.
It connects continental movement, ocean basin formation, earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain building.
The Earth's rigid lithosphere is broken into plates that move over the semi-fluid asthenosphere.
Plate movements are driven by internal heat-driven processes within the Earth.
